la:adj:brevis.html:
brĕvis, e, adj. (abl. breve, ;
comp. abl. breviore, ) [cf. βραχύς, ], short, little, of small extent, in space and time (opp. longus; in space, in good class. prose, diff. from parvus, which designates that which fills a small space in length, breadth, and thickness; while brevis is used only of length in its different directions of breadth, height, or depth; and even of a circle, as merely a line, and without reference to the space enclosed, v.infra. In poets and postAug. prose brevis sometimes = parvus).
Lit., in space.
In distance, extent, short, little, small, narrow (opp. latus), : brevior via,; : via brevis,; ; : cursus brevissimus,: brevius iter,: cursu brevissimus Almo,: quid mihi, quod lato non separor aequore, prodest? Num minus haec nobis tam brevis obstat aqua?so narrow a stream,; cf. also brevis unda, opp. latum mare, and 142: non Asiam brevioris aquae disterminat usquam fluctus ab Europā, (strictioris, Schol.); cf. : brevissima terra,: in Euboico scopulus brevis emicat altō Gurgite,a small, narrow rock,: brevibus Gyaris,: scis In breve te cogi (sc. libellum),that you are closely rolled together,: quo brevius valent,the nearer, the more powerful are they in conflict,.—
Trop. of the journey of life: quid est, quod in hoc tam exiguo vitae curriculo et tam brevi tantis nos in laboribus exerceamus?; cf.: vitae brevis cursus, gloriae sempiternus,: tum brevior dirae mortis aperta via est,.—And poet. of the thread of life: fila vitae breviora,. —
In height, short, small, low (opp. altus and sometimes longus); of the human figure: sed sedebat judex L. Aurifex, brevior ipse quam testis,: ut statura breves in digitos eriguntur,: forma,: (puella) longa brevisque,: brevis corpore,; id. Vit. Hor.—Of a maiden changed to a boy: et incomptis brevior mensura capillis,.— Of other things: ut pleraque Alpium ab Italiā sicut breviora, ita arrectiora sunt,lower,: brevior ilex,: mus,little,. —
In depth, small, little, shallow (opp. profundus): puteus,: vada,; .—Hence, subst.: brĕvia, ium, n., as in Gr. τὰ βραχέα, shallow places, shallows, shoals: tris Eurus ab alto In brevia et syrtis urget, (brevia vadosa dicit, per quae vadi pedibus potest, Serv.); : neque discerni poterant incerta ab solidis, brevia a profundis, : brevia litorum,fin.—Perh. also in sing.: breve, Draeg. ad loc. (Ritter, brevia; al. breve litus).—
Trop.: brevia, in quibus volutatur, incerta, ancipitia,difficulties,.—
Of the line of a circle: ubi circulus (i.e. arcticus) axem Ultimus extremum spatioque brevissimus ambit,makes the shortest path,; cf. of similar orbits, of stars: absides breviores,. 15, 13, § 63.—Of the circular course of a horse on the track: discit gyro breviore flecti,. —
Transf., of time.
Lit. (the usu. signif. of the word), short, brief, small, little.
In gen.: quanto, nox, fuisti longior hac proxumā, Tanto brevior dies ut fiat faciam,: breve spatium'st perferundi quae minitas mihi,: brevis hora,; so : Pa. Brevin' an longinquo sermone? Mi. Tribus verbis, : occasio,; : brevis hic est fructus homulleis,short is this enjoyment for little men,; cf.: MORS. PERFECIT. TVA. VT. TIBE. ESSENT. OMNIA. BREVIA. HONOS. FAMA. VIRTVSQVE. GLORIA. ATQVE. INGENIVM.,: omnia brevia tolerabilia esse debent,; ; ; ; : quoniam vita brevis est, memoriam nostri quam maxime longam efficere,; so, vitae summa brevis spem nos vetat incohare longam,; cf. : aut omnia breviora aliquanto fuere, aut Saguntum principio anni captum,occupied a shorter time,: brevissimum tempus,: detrimentum,: arbitrium mortis,: breves populi Romani amores,: tempus,: nobis quom semel occidit brevis lux, nox est perpetua una dormienda,: fructus,: aevum,; ; ; : anni,: ver,; : flores rosae,quickly withering, short-lived,: lilium,: cena,frugal,: mensa,: dominus,living but a short time,: stultitia,: ira furor brevis est,: actio brevis atque concisa,: somnus,: nec gratius quicquam decore nec brevius,nothing is more acceptable, but nothing more perishable, fading, than beauty,: domus,: fortuna,.—
Esp.
Comp. brevius, with subj. clause, shorter, i.e. easier, more convenient: brevius visum urbana crimina incipi, quorum obvii testes erant,: modo ne existimes brevius esse ab urbe mitti, Trag. ap. (49), 3.—
In brevi spatio, brevi spatio, in brevi tempore, brevi tempore, and absol. brevi or in brevi, in a short time, shortly (before or after) (brevi tempore and brevi are class.; the latter, as in Gr. ἐν βραχεῖ, to be considered as neuter, without supplying tempore): inque brevi spatio mutantur saecla animantum,; so ; ; ; cf.: in multo breviore temporis spatio,: multa brevi spatio simulacra geruntur,; : spatio brevi,: res publica per vos brevi tempore jus suum recuperabit,; ; ; ; ; ; : sic ille affectus, brevi postea est mortuus,soon after, (Zumpt; acc. to MSS. perbrevi).—So brevi post = paulo post: brevi post Marcellus Romam venit,; : brevi deinde,: (Britanni) tantum usu cotidiano et exercitatione efficiunt, uti in declivi ac praecipiti loco incitatos equos sustinere et brevi (in a short time, i.e. with great rapidity) moderari ac flectere consuerint, Herz. and Held.: fama tanti facinoris per omnem Africam brevi divolgatur,; : mirantur tam brevi rem Romanam crevisse,: brevi omnia subegit,; so ; ; ; ; : scire in brevi, Afran. ap. P.; .—
Brevi, a short time, a little while:

cunctatusque brevi, contortam viribus hastam in Persea misit, ; cf.: illa brevi spatio silet,; so, * breve,.—

Ad breve, for a short time, ; cf.: ad breve quoddam tempus,.—
Transf. to things done or taking place in a short time; so most freq.
Of discourse, short, brief, concise (most freq. in Cic. and Quint.): narratio,; : laudatio; comprehensio et ambitus ille verborum erat apud illum contractus et brevis,; cf. : nunc venio ad illa tua brevia: et primum illud, quo nihil potest esse brevius: bonum omne laudabile, etc.,: quam falsa re! quam brevia responsu!: urbanitas est virtus quaedam in breve dictum coacta, Dom. Mars. ap. : Homerus brevem eloquentiam Menelao dedit, (brevis = οὐ πολύμυθος, Hom. Il. 3, 214): breviores commentarii,: annotatio,: brevia illa atque concisa,; so, sententiae,: causae,: docendi compendia,: comprehensiones,: quod ut brevissimo pateat exemplo,: commendatio, requiring few words, i.e. moderate, .— Meton. of a speaker or orator, brief: multos imitatio brevitatis decipit, ut cum se breves putent esse, longissimi sint,: brevior in scribendo,: brevis esse laboro, Obscurus fio,: in eloquendo brevis,: densus et brevis et semper instans sibi Thucydides,.—Hence, brĕvī, adv., briefly, in few words (freq. and class.): brevi pro breviter M. Tullius de Orat. ad Quintum fratrem (1, 8, 34): ac ne plura quidem quae sunt innumerabilia consecter, comprehendam brevi, P.: id percurram brevi,: aliquid explicare, Wund.: circumscribere et definire,; so Orell. N. cr.; : complecti,: exponere,: reprehendere,: reddere,: respondere,: perscribere,; so ; ; cf.: in brevi,.—So once in epistolary style: breve facere, to be short or brief: quid scribam? breve faciam,; cf.: longum est ea dicere, sed hoc breve dicam,.—Once, in breve cogere (diff. from I. A.), to comprise in few words, bring into a small compass: in breve coactae causae,; cf.: in breve coactio causae,.— In late Lat. subst.: brĕvis, is, m. (sc. liber—acc. to another reading, brĕve, is, n.), a short catalogue, summary, = breviarium: brevis nominum,; so ; ; , n. 2 al.—
Of a short syllable; rarely as adj.: Syllaba longa brevi subjecta vocatur iambus,: a brevis, gre brevis, faciet tamen longam priorem, et saep.—More freq. subst.: brĕvis, is, f. (sc. syllaba): dactylus, qui est e longā et duabus brevibus,: in fine pro longā accipi brevem,; : plurimum habent celeritatis breves,.— Hence also once of a syllable long by position, but pronounced short: indoctus dicimus brevi primā litterā, insanus productā: inhumanus brevi, infelix longā, Meyer N. cr.; cf. sqq., and Schütz Lex. Cic. s. v. brevis.—
For parvus, exiguus, little, small: exigua pars brevisque,: Canidia brevibus implicata viperis,: Alecto brevibus torquata colubris,: brevi latere ac pede longo est,; cf. just before: breve quod caput, ardua cervix, v. 89, and brevis alvus, (on the other hand, : parvae alvi): mus,: forma (sc. pueri in stellionem mutati),.— So, lapathi herba, (brevis = parva, non excrescens in altum, Schol. Cruqu.): folia breviora, (minor corona, Schol. Cruqu.): census,: pondus,: impensa, Ruhnk.: sigillum,: insulae,; cf. : vasculum, : offulae,: pantheris in candido breves macularum oculi,.—With nom. abstr.: breve in exiguo marmore nomen ero,; .—So, pondus, —Hence, brĕ-vĭter, adv., shortly, briefly, etc.
Of space (acc. to I.) (rare): seu libeat, curvo brevius convertere gyro, shorter, i. e. in a smaller circle, : parvo brevius quam totus,a little less than the whole,: Sarmatae, omisso arcu, quo brevius valent, contis gladiisque ruerent,.—Far more freq. in prose and poetry,
(Acc. to II. A. b. and c.) Of time, in a short time.
In gen.: iratum breviter vites, inimicum diu, Publ. Syr. v. 249 Rib.: sapiens, cum breviter et strictim colore atque vultu motus est,.—
Esp.
In expression, briefly, in brief, in few words, concisely, summarily: sed breviter paucis praestat comprendere multa,: multa breviter et commode dicta (sc. ἀποφθέγματα; cf. ) memoriae mandabam, : rem totam breviter cognoscite,; ; so : summatim breviterque describere,: breviter tangere, Beier N. cr.: breviter et modice disserere,: adicere aliquid,; cf. also ; ; ; : omnia soli Forsan Pacuvio breviter dabit (i.e. paucis testamenti verbis, quibus heres ex asse scribetur), Web. (cf. : beatum exiguis tabulis).—Comp., ; , prooem. § 1; 8, 6, 61; 9, 2, 16; 10, 1, 49; 11, 1, 5 al.—Sup., ; ; ; —
Of syllables: quibus in verbis eae primae litterae sunt quae in sapiente atque felice, producte dicitur, in ceteris omnibus breviter,.
